#!/usr/bin/env python3
r"""Build the layout that the rest of the pipeline analyses.

This script is the stand-in for drawing a board by hand. A later project
can start from a KiCad schematic, assign footprints, and route the copper.
The export below does not care how the board was drawn. It only needs a
.kicad_pcb and a net name.

What this file produces is the layout only. It does not solve current or
temperature. The copper solid that Salome meshes comes from the next
command, run in the KiCad 9 container from this directory:

    kicad-cli pcb export xao --output trace.xao \
        --no-board-body --no-components \
        --include-tracks --include-pads --include-zones \
        --fuse-shapes --net-filter TRACE trace.kicad_pcb

--no-board-body leaves the FR4 out. --fuse-shapes joins the pads, tracks,
and via into one solid. --net-filter TRACE drops every other net. A thermal
model needs the dielectric as its own solid, so that export would keep the
board body. This current-only model does not.

Geometry, millimetres, board origin at the lower left:
  outline 12 x 8 on Edge.Cuts (not in the XAO)
  pad A   F.Cu  2 x 2 at (3, 4)     net TRACE
  track   F.Cu  0.4 wide, (3, 4) to (6, 4)
  via     through, drill 0.3, pad 0.6, at (6, 4)
  track   B.Cu  0.4 wide, (6, 4) to (9, 4)
  pad B   B.Cu  2 x 2 at (9, 4)     net TRACE

Copper thickness is written into the stackup as 0.035 mm (1 oz).
Running the script again replaces trace.kicad_pcb and gives the objects
new ids.
"""
import pathlib
import pcbnew


def say(line):
    # One line of the run log. Flushed so a piped capture keeps the order.
    print(line, flush=True)


# Board file written beside this script. pcbnew is the KiCad 9 Python module,
# so this runs inside the KiCad environment, not the system interpreter.
OUT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "trace.kicad_pcb"
say(f"KiCad pcbnew {pcbnew.Version()}")
say(f"Writing the layout to {OUT}")
say("This step draws copper only. It does not export the XAO or solve a field.")


def mm(v):
    # KiCad stores coordinates as integer nanometres. FromMM does that conversion.
    return pcbnew.FromMM(v)


def xy(x, y):
    # One board point. x grows right and y grows down, origin at the lower left
    # of the outline drawn below.
    return pcbnew.VECTOR2I(mm(x), mm(y))


# Create an empty two-layer board at the output path.
board = pcbnew.NewBoard(str(OUT))
settings = board.GetDesignSettings()
# F.Cu and B.Cu. A later thermal model still wants this layer count, plus the
# dielectric between them.
settings.SetCopperLayerCount(2)
# Finished board thickness, copper plus core. The core thickness is written
# into the stackup text after the save.
settings.SetBoardThickness(mm(1.6))
say("Board has 2 copper layers and a finished thickness of 1.6 mm.")

# One net. The XAO export keeps copper whose net name matches TRACE.
net = pcbnew.NETINFO_ITEM(board, "TRACE")
board.Add(net)
say("Added net TRACE. The XAO export keeps copper on this net and drops the rest.")


def edge(x1, y1, x2, y2):
    # One straight segment of the board outline. Edge.Cuts is the KiCad layer
    # for that outline. The current XAO export skips it because the board body
    # is turned off. Draw it anyway so the file is a real board, and so a later
    # export can turn the outline into an FR4 solid.
    shape = pcbnew.PCB_SHAPE(board)
    shape.SetShape(pcbnew.SHAPE_T_SEGMENT)
    shape.SetLayer(pcbnew.Edge_Cuts)
    shape.SetStart(xy(x1, y1))
    shape.SetEnd(xy(x2, y2))
    # Line width of the outline graphic, not a copper width.
    shape.SetWidth(mm(0.05))
    board.Add(shape)


# Close the 12 mm by 8 mm rectangle. The last segment returns to the first point.
edge(0, 0, 12, 0)
edge(12, 0, 12, 8)
edge(12, 8, 0, 8)
edge(0, 8, 0, 0)
say("Outline is a 12 mm by 8 mm rectangle on Edge.Cuts. The current XAO export leaves this outline out.")

# KiCad stores pads inside a footprint. J1 is that holder. Both pads share it,
# so the XAO face names contain J1: Pad_F_J1_A_TRACE and Pad_B_J1_B_TRACE.
fp = pcbnew.FOOTPRINT(board)
fp.SetReference("J1")
fp.SetValue("trace-pads")
fp.SetPosition(xy(0, 0))
board.Add(fp)
say("Footprint J1 holds both pads. KiCad will name the XAO faces from J1, the pad, and the net.")


def smd_pad(number, layer, x, y):
    # A surface pad on one copper layer. number becomes the pad name in the
    # XAO group. The pad is the face Elmer will drive or sink.
    pad = pcbnew.PAD(fp)
    pad.SetNumber(number)
    pad.SetName(number)
    # SMD keeps the pad on the single layer selected below. A through-hole pad
    # would also drill the board, which this terminal does not do.
    pad.SetAttribute(pcbnew.PAD_ATTRIB_SMD)
    pad.SetShape(pcbnew.PAD_SHAPE_RECT)
    # 2 mm by 2 mm. Salome reports the face area as 4 mm^2.
    pad.SetSize(pcbnew.VECTOR2I(mm(2.0), mm(2.0)))
    # The layer set says which copper sheet the pad occupies. SetLayer is the
    # pad's primary layer and must name the same sheet.
    layers = pcbnew.LSET()
    layers.AddLayer(layer)
    pad.SetLayerSet(layers)
    pad.SetLayer(layer)
    # (x, y) is the pad center, not a corner.
    pad.SetPosition(xy(x, y))
    pad.SetNet(net)
    fp.Add(pad)
    return pad


# Front terminal at the left, back terminal at the right.
smd_pad("A", pcbnew.F_Cu, 3.0, 4.0)
say("Pad A is 2 mm by 2 mm on F.Cu, centered at (3 mm, 4 mm), on net TRACE.")
smd_pad("B", pcbnew.B_Cu, 9.0, 4.0)
say("Pad B is 2 mm by 2 mm on B.Cu, centered at (9 mm, 4 mm), on net TRACE.")


def track(layer, x1, y1, x2, y2, width):
    # A straight copper trace. The centerline runs from (x1, y1) to (x2, y2),
    # and width is the copper width across that line. These 0.4 mm traces are
    # the narrow part of the path, so the current density and the heating peak
    # there.
    item = pcbnew.PCB_TRACK(board)
    item.SetStart(xy(x1, y1))
    item.SetEnd(xy(x2, y2))
    item.SetWidth(mm(width))
    item.SetLayer(layer)
    item.SetNet(net)
    board.Add(item)


# Front trace from pad A to the via, then back trace from the via to pad B.
track(pcbnew.F_Cu, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0, 4.0, 0.4)
say("Front trace is 0.4 mm wide on F.Cu, from (3 mm, 4 mm) to the via at (6 mm, 4 mm).")
track(pcbnew.B_Cu, 6.0, 4.0, 9.0, 4.0, 0.4)
say("Back trace is 0.4 mm wide on B.Cu, from the via at (6 mm, 4 mm) to (9 mm, 4 mm).")

# The via is the copper barrel that joins the front trace to the back trace.
# Drill is the hole. Width is the annular pad diameter. A through via spans
# F.Cu to B.Cu, so the fused XAO solid is one conductor.
via = pcbnew.PCB_VIA(board)
via.SetPosition(xy(6.0, 4.0))
via.SetDrill(mm(0.3))
via.SetWidth(mm(0.6))
via.SetViaType(pcbnew.VIATYPE_THROUGH)
via.SetLayerPair(pcbnew.F_Cu, pcbnew.B_Cu)
via.SetNet(net)
board.Add(via)
say("Through via at (6 mm, 4 mm): drill 0.3 mm, pad 0.6 mm, from F.Cu to B.Cu, on net TRACE.")

# Write the board KiCad can open. The stackup thicknesses are not part of that
# save in this pcbnew binding, so they are inserted into the file text next.
pcbnew.SaveBoard(str(OUT), board)
text = OUT.read_text()
# 0.035 mm is 1 oz copper on each outer layer. 1.53 mm of FR4 fills the rest
# of the 1.6 mm board. The dielectric line records the board for a later
# thermal model. This XAO export does not turn that line into a solid.
stackup = """\t\t(stackup
\t\t\t(layer "F.Cu" (type "copper") (thickness 0.035))
\t\t\t(layer "dielectric 1" (type "core") (thickness 1.53) (material "FR4") (epsilon_r 4.5) (loss_tangent 0.02))
\t\t\t(layer "B.Cu" (type "copper") (thickness 0.035))
\t\t\t(copper_finish "None")
\t\t\t(dielectric_constraints no)
\t\t)
"""
# Insert the stackup once, directly under the setup block KiCad already wrote.
needle = "\t(setup\n"
if needle not in text:
    raise SystemExit("setup section not found")
text = text.replace(needle, needle + stackup, 1)
OUT.write_text(text)
say("Stackup written under setup: F.Cu 0.035 mm copper, 1.53 mm FR4 core, B.Cu 0.035 mm copper.")
say(f"Wrote {OUT.name}: {OUT.stat().st_size} bytes.")
say("Next command is the XAO export. It fuses the TRACE copper and leaves the FR4 behind.")
say("  kicad-cli pcb export xao --output trace.xao --no-board-body --no-components \\")
say("      --include-tracks --include-pads --include-zones --fuse-shapes \\")
say("      --net-filter TRACE trace.kicad_pcb")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn the KiCad XAO into a volume mesh Elmer can read.

Place in the pipeline, after trace.xao exists and before ElmerGrid:

    salome shell -- python3 mesh_trace.py
    ElmerGrid 8 2 trace.unv -scale 1.0e-3 1.0e-3 1.0e-3 -out mesh

Use Salome's Python. The system interpreter has no salome module. The
shell command needs the "--" so Salome does not drop the script name.

The XAO coordinates are millimetres, and so are the mesh sizes below.
ElmerGrid's scale of 0.001 is what converts the mesh to metres. Skip that
scale and the conductivity and the current density are applied to a board
a thousand times too large.

The mesh groups are renamed input and output. case.sif attaches the 12 V
pad and the current sink to those names. A different board can use this
same script once its pad-face names are set in FRONT and BACK.

This step does not compute temperature. It only fills the copper with
tetrahedra. Heating is computed later from the current.
"""
import os
import sys

import salome

# Start a Salome session in this process. geomBuilder and smeshBuilder import
# only after that session exists.
salome.salome_init()
from salome.geom import geomBuilder
from salome.smesh import smeshBuilder
import SMESH

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
XAO = os.path.join(HERE, "trace.xao")
UNV = os.path.join(HERE, "trace.unv")
LOG = os.path.join(HERE, "mesh_trace.log")

# Each pair is (maximum element size, minimum element size) in millimetres.
# The first pair is the one this board accepted. The minimum, 0.08 mm, is
# thicker than the 0.035 mm foil. Netgen still built a volume mesh. The later
# pairs are finer fallbacks for a board where the coarse pair produces no
# tetrahedra. SetFineness(5) below means "custom", so these two numbers are
# the ones Netgen uses.
CANDIDATES = (
    (0.20, 0.08),
    (0.10, 0.02),
    (0.05, 0.01),
    (0.035, 0.008),
)

# Face names KiCad wrote into the XAO. They name the front and back pads.
# mesh.GroupOnGeom copies them onto the mesh as input and output.
FRONT = "Pad_F_J1_A_TRACE"
BACK = "Pad_B_J1_B_TRACE"


def log(line):
    # Print and keep a copy. Salome's own console is easy to lose.
    print(line, flush=True)
    with open(LOG, "a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(line + "\n")


def main():
    # Start a fresh log so a failed size is not mixed with an older run.
    if os.path.exists(LOG):
        os.remove(LOG)
    # geompy reads and measures the CAD solid. smesh meshes it.
    geompy = geomBuilder.New()
    smesh = smeshBuilder.New()

    # ImportXAO returns the solid, any sub-shapes, the named groups, and
    # fields. This file has one solid and two face groups. The fields are
    # unused. ok is false when the file is not a readable XAO.
    ok, shape, _sub, groups, _fields = geompy.ImportXAO(XAO)
    if not ok:
        raise SystemExit("ImportXAO failed for " + XAO)
    # Publish the solid in the Salome study under the name "trace".
    geompy.addToStudy(shape, "trace")
    log(f"Imported {os.path.basename(XAO)}.")
    log("The file holds one fused copper solid and the named pad faces. There is no FR4 in it.")
    # Box of the solid in millimetres. KiCad's Y axis is flipped in the
    # OpenCASCADE solid, so a board drawn at positive y can show a negative
    # y here. The log is the check that the export landed where expected.
    xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax = geompy.BoundingBox(shape)
    log(
        "Bounding box of the solid, millimetres: "
        f"x from {xmin:.6g} to {xmax:.6g}, "
        f"y from {ymin:.6g} to {ymax:.6g}, "
        f"z from {zmin:.6g} to {zmax:.6g}."
    )
    log("KiCad's Y axis is flipped in this solid, so the pads sit at negative y.")

    # Measure every named face. area from BasicProperties is mm^2. Elmer's
    # current density is A/m^2, and 1 mm^2 = 1e-6 m^2. For this board each
    # pad is 4 mm^2, so 0.5 A leaving the pad is -0.5/4e-6 = -125000 A/m^2.
    # A new board needs that division repeated. Do not reuse 125000.
    by_name = {}
    for group in groups:
        name = group.GetName()
        by_name[name] = group
        geompy.addToStudyInFather(shape, group, name)
        length, area, volume = geompy.BasicProperties(group)
        area_m2 = area * 1.0e-6
        log(
            f"Group {name}: length {length:.6g} mm, "
            f"area {area:.6g} mm^2 ({area_m2:.6g} m^2), "
            f"volume {volume:.6g} mm^3."
        )
        if name == BACK and area_m2 > 0.0:
            # 0.5 A leaves through the output pad. Negative density is the
            # Elmer sign for current leaving the solid. A new board must
            # recompute this from the measured area.
            density = -0.5 / area_m2
            log(
                "  The output pad sinks 0.5 A, so the boundary current density "
                f"is {density:.6g} A/m^2. case.sif must use this value."
            )

    if FRONT not in by_name or BACK not in by_name:
        raise SystemExit("pad groups missing: " + ", ".join(sorted(by_name)))

    chosen = None
    mesh = None
    for max_mm, min_mm in CANDIDATES:
        # A new mesh object for this size pair. The name records the sizes
        # that were tried.
        mesh = smesh.Mesh(shape, f"trace_{max_mm}_{min_mm}")
        # Netgen 1D-2D-3D builds the edges, then the surface triangles, then
        # the tetrahedra. One algorithm owns all three.
        algo = mesh.Tetrahedron(algo=smeshBuilder.NETGEN_1D2D3D)
        # 5 is Netgen's custom fineness. Without it, SetMaxSize is ignored.
        algo.SetFineness(5)
        algo.SetMaxSize(max_mm)
        algo.SetMinSize(min_mm)
        # Linear tetrahedra have four nodes. Elmer's static-current solver
        # uses those. Second order would add mid-edge nodes and a much
        # larger system.
        algo.SetSecondOrder(False)
        # Copy each pad face onto the mesh and rename it. SMESH.FACE means
        # the group is a surface. Elmer boundary conditions can only target
        # a surface group. The names input and output must match case.sif.
        input_group = mesh.GroupOnGeom(by_name[FRONT], "input", SMESH.FACE)
        output_group = mesh.GroupOnGeom(by_name[BACK], "output", SMESH.FACE)
        log(
            f"Meshing with Netgen 1D-2D-3D. Maximum element {max_mm} mm, "
            f"minimum element {min_mm} mm, linear tetrahedra."
        )
        if min_mm > 0.035:
            log(
                f"  The minimum size {min_mm} mm is thicker than the "
                "0.035 mm foil. Netgen can still fill this solid."
            )
        computed = mesh.Compute()
        volumes = mesh.NbVolumes()
        log(
            f"  Compute returned {computed}. "
            f"Nodes {mesh.NbNodes()}, faces {mesh.NbFaces()}, "
            f"tetrahedra {volumes}."
        )
        # A mesh with no tetrahedra is not a copper volume. Try the next,
        # finer pair. GetLog keeps Netgen's reason.
        if not computed or volumes == 0:
            for err in mesh.GetLog():
                log("  " + str(err))
            continue
        log(
            f"  Mesh group input ({FRONT}) has {input_group.Size()} faces. "
            f"Mesh group output ({BACK}) has {output_group.Size()} faces."
        )
        log("  Those two names are the boundary names in case.sif.")
        chosen = (max_mm, min_mm)
        break

    if chosen is None:
        raise SystemExit("no volume mesh; see " + LOG)

    # ExportUNV writes trace.unv and returns None even when the file is good.
    # The header of that file says the units are metres, but the node
    # coordinates are still millimetres. ElmerGrid must scale them.
    mesh.ExportUNV(UNV)
    if not os.path.isfile(UNV) or os.path.getsize(UNV) < 1000:
        raise SystemExit("ExportUNV failed")
    log(
        f"Wrote {os.path.basename(UNV)} ({os.path.getsize(UNV)} bytes) "
        f"with element sizes {chosen[0]} mm maximum and {chosen[1]} mm minimum."
    )
    log("The UNV header says metres, but the node coordinates are still millimetres.")
    log("Next command: ElmerGrid 8 2 trace.unv -scale 1.0e-3 1.0e-3 1.0e-3 -out mesh")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except SystemExit:
        raise
    except Exception:
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        sys.exit(1)

Imported trace.xao.
The file holds one fused copper solid and the named pad faces. There is no FR4 in it.

! Static current in the copper of trace.kicad_pcb.
! This case does not solve temperature. Calculate Joule Heating stores the
! volumetric heating, in W/m^3, that a later heat case would use as its source.
! A temperature solution also needs the FR4 solid, which this mesh does not have.
!
! Mesh coordinates are metres. ElmerGrid scaled the Salome UNV by 0.001.
! The output pad area measured in Salome is 4.0e-6 m^2. Current of 0.5 A
! leaves that face, so the applied density is -0.5/4.0e-6 = -125000 A/m^2.
! Measure the pad again before reusing this number on another board.

Header
  ! Mesh directory written by ElmerGrid. "." is the directory that holds this file.
  Mesh DB "." "mesh"
End

Simulation
  ! 5 prints the linear iterations and the post-processing fields.
  Max Output Level = 5
  Coordinate System = Cartesian
  ! One solution of the steady current problem. There is no time step.
  Simulation Type = Steady State
  Steady State Max Iterations = 1
  ! Write the result on the only iteration.
  Output Intervals(1) = 1
  ! Elmer appends the step, so the file on disk is case_t0001.vtu.
  Post File = case.vtu
End

Body 1
  ! ElmerGrid renames the single copper volume. Salome had one solid, and the
  ! UNV physical index collided with a group index, so the body id became 3.
  ! Name and Target Bodies must both point at that id. Check mesh.names if a
  ! new mesh is numbered differently.
  Name = body3
  Target Bodies(1) = 3
  Equation = 1
  Material = 1
End

Solver 1
  ! Static current continuity. The unknown is the electric potential, in volts.
  ! Current density follows from the conductivity and the potential gradient.
  Equation = "Stat Current Solver"
  Procedure = "StatCurrentSolve" "StatCurrentSolver"
  Variable = Potential
  ! Nodal current vector, A/m^2. The narrow 0.4 mm traces hold the peak.
  Calculate Volume Current = True
  ! Nodal heating, W/m^3. This is sigma times the square of the electric field.
  ! It is a result of this solve, not a temperature.
  Calculate Joule Heating = True
  Linear System Solver = Iterative
  ! BiCGStab with ILU1 reached 3.75e-11 in 27 iterations on this mesh.
  Linear System Iterative Method = BiCGStab
  Linear System Preconditioning = ILU1
  Linear System Max Iterations = 500
  Linear System Convergence Tolerance = 1.0e-10
  ! Print the residual every 20 iterations, and on the iteration that converges.
  Linear System Residual Output = 20
  Steady State Convergence Tolerance = 1.0e-8
End

Equation 1
  ! The copper body runs solver 1 and no other solver.
  Active Solvers(1) = 1
End

Material 1
  ! Generic copper, S/m. No thermal conductivity is set, because this solver
  ! does not use one.
  Electric Conductivity = 47.00e6
End

Boundary Condition 1
  ! The front pad. Mesh group "input" is boundary 1 in mesh.names.
  Name = input
  Target Boundaries(1) = 1
  ! Fixed potential. The other pad is not fixed, so the drop is a result.
  Potential = 12.0
End

Boundary Condition 2
  ! The back pad. Mesh group "output" is boundary 2.
  ! Negative density means current leaves the copper. Positive would inject it.
  Name = output
  Target Boundaries(1) = 2
  Current Density = -125000.0
End

draws the potential and Joule-heating figures. It uses the ParaView build on the host display.

"""Draw the potential and the Joule heating from Elmer's VTU file.

This is the last step of the current-conduction pipeline. case_t0001.vtu
must already exist beside this script. The pictures are the two figures
on the page. Nothing here changes the solution.

The ParaView 5.10 build in openfoam/openfoam11-paraview510 is an X11
program. It has to run as the desktop user and see the host display.
Forcing offscreen rendering crashes it in XSync. From this directory:

    docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -e HOME=/tmp -e DISPLAY=:0 \
      -e XAUTHORITY=/tmp/.Xauthority \
      -v "$HOME/.Xauthority:/tmp/.Xauthority:ro" \
      -v /tmp/.X11-unix:/tmp/.X11-unix -v "$PWD":/work \
      --entrypoint bash openfoam/openfoam11-paraview510 \
      -lc '/opt/paraviewopenfoam510/bin/pvpython /work/render_views.py'

A later heat solution would be drawn by pointing this same script at the
heat case's VTU and naming the temperature field. This file draws the
current-case fields only.
"""
import os

from paraview.simple import (
    ColorBy,
    GetActiveCamera,
    GetActiveViewOrCreate,
    GetColorTransferFunction,
    GetScalarBar,
    HideScalarBarIfNotNeeded,
    LoadPalette,
    Render,
    ResetCamera,
    SaveScreenshot,
    Show,
    XMLUnstructuredGridReader,
)
from paraview import servermanager

def say(line):
    print(line, flush=True)


HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
# Elmer wrote this into the mesh directory. It was copied here next to the page.
VTU = os.path.join(HERE, "case_t0001.vtu")
OUT = os.path.join(HERE, "images")
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

say(f"Reading {os.path.basename(VTU)}.")
# Read the unstructured tetrahedra and the nodal fields.
reader = XMLUnstructuredGridReader(FileName=[VTU])
reader.UpdatePipeline()
# Fetch pulls the dataset out of the server so the ranges can be printed.
# The picture itself is drawn from reader, not from this fetched copy.
fetched = servermanager.Fetch(reader)
point_data = fetched.GetPointData()
names = [point_data.GetArrayName(i) for i in range(point_data.GetNumberOfArrays())]
say(
    f"VTU has {fetched.GetNumberOfPoints()} points and "
    f"{fetched.GetNumberOfCells()} cells."
)
say("Point fields: " + ", ".join(names) + ".")
say("Drawing potential and Joule heating. This script does not solve either field.")


def field_range(name):
    # GetRange on a scalar array is (min, max). On the three-component
    # "volume current" array it is the range of the first component only,
    # which is not the magnitude. The loop at the bottom computes that.
    array = fetched.GetPointData().GetArray(name)
    return array.GetRange()


view = GetActiveViewOrCreate("RenderView")
# The default palette is dark. The page figures need a white sheet.
LoadPalette("WhiteBackground")
# Wide frame so the color bar can sit in the empty region to the right.
view.ViewSize = [1700, 950]
# The corner triad overlaps the copper at this zoom.
view.OrientationAxesVisibility = 0

display = Show(reader, view)
# Surface paints the outside of the tetrahedra. The foil is thin, so the
# outside shows the pads, the traces, and the via barrel.
display.Representation = "Surface"

# Fit the copper, then look down at an angle so both pads and the via read
# as separate objects. The window center shifts the copper toward the left
# so the legend is not drawn on top of the output pad.
ResetCamera(view)
camera = GetActiveCamera()
camera.Azimuth(35)
camera.Elevation(25)
ResetCamera(view)
camera.Zoom(1.15)
camera.SetWindowCenter(0.28, 0.0)
say("Camera azimuth 35 degrees, elevation 25 degrees. The copper is shifted left to leave room for the legend.")


def save(field, filename, title):
    # Color the surface by this nodal field.
    ColorBy(display, ("POINTS", field))
    # Stretch the color scale across this field's own min and max.
    # The potential only falls 3.35 mV, so its bar runs from about
    # 11.997 V to 12 V, not from 0 V to 12 V.
    display.RescaleTransferFunctionToDataRange(False, True)
    # Drop both bars before showing the one for this field. Leaving the
    # potential bar up puts its tick labels on the heating figure.
    HideScalarBarIfNotNeeded(GetColorTransferFunction("potential"), view)
    HideScalarBarIfNotNeeded(GetColorTransferFunction("joule heating"), view)
    display.SetScalarBarVisibility(view, True)
    lut = GetColorTransferFunction(field)
    bar = GetScalarBar(lut, view)
    bar.Title = title
    # A scalar field has no component title. An empty string suppresses it.
    bar.ComponentTitle = ""
    bar.TitleColor = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    bar.LabelColor = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    # Place the bar by hand, in the open margin to the right of the copper.
    # "Any Location" lets Position take effect. Position is the lower-left
    # corner of the bar in fractions of the view.
    bar.WindowLocation = "Any Location"
    bar.Position = [0.90, 0.16]
    bar.ScalarBarLength = 0.68
    Render(view)
    path = os.path.join(OUT, filename)
    SaveScreenshot(path, view, ImageResolution=[1700, 950])
    low, high = field_range(field)
    say(f"Saved {filename}.")
    say(f"  {title}: minimum {low:.8g}, maximum {high:.8g}.")
    say("  The color bar is in the right margin, clear of the copper.")
    say(f"  File: images/{filename}")


save("potential", "potential.png", "Electric potential (V)")
save("joule heating", "joule_heating.png", "Joule heating (W/m^3)")
# Report the vector range too. GetRange here is one component, so the next
# loop is the magnitude a reader should compare with the 0.4 mm trace.
current = field_range("volume current")
say(
    "Volume current is a 3-component vector. VTK's range on that array is "
    f"the first component only: {current[0]:.8g} to {current[1]:.8g} A/m^2."
)
mag = fetched.GetPointData().GetArray("volume current")
lo = 1.0e300
hi = 0.0
for i in range(mag.GetNumberOfTuples()):
    x, y, z = mag.GetTuple(i)
    value = (x * x + y * y + z * z) ** 0.5
    if value < lo:
        lo = value
    if value > hi:
        hi = value
say(f"Volume-current magnitude over the nodes: {lo:.8g} to {hi:.8g} A/m^2.")
say("A 0.5 A current in a 0.4 mm by 0.035 mm section is about 3.57e7 A/m^2.")
